findings.title: Data read + external network = exfiltration path
findings.description: Tools that can read internal data AND make external network requests create a direct exfiltration channel. A hijacked agent could read sensitive data then forward it to an attacker-controlled endpoint. Provided by: get-annotated-message, get-env, get-header-params, get-resource-links, get-resource-reference, get-roots-list, get-structured-content, get-sum, get-tiny-image, gzip-file-as-resource, simulate-research-query, trigger-list-changed, trigger-resource-update (data_read) + trigger-elicitation-request-async, trigger-elicitation-request, trigger-sampling-request-async, trigger-sampling-request, trigger-url-elicitation (network_external).
findings.recommendation: Implement tool-level permission scoping. Consider whether both capabilities are necessary or if one can be restricted.

findings.title: Code execution + external network = remote code execution path
findings.description: Tools that execute code AND fetch external content can download and run attacker-controlled payloads. Provided by: trigger-long-running-operation (code_execute) + trigger-elicitation-request-async, trigger-elicitation-request, trigger-sampling-request-async, trigger-sampling-request, trigger-url-elicitation (network_external).
findings.recommendation: Implement tool-level permission scoping. Consider whether both capabilities are necessary or if one can be restricted.

findings.title: Broad data read + write = data manipulation risk
findings.description: Tools that can both read and write data could be manipulated to corrupt, overwrite, or delete information. Provided by: get-annotated-message, get-env, get-header-params, get-resource-links, get-resource-reference, get-roots-list, get-structured-content, get-sum, get-tiny-image, gzip-file-as-resource, simulate-research-query, trigger-list-changed, trigger-resource-update (data_read) + toggle-subscriber-updates, trigger-resource-update (data_write).
findings.recommendation: Implement tool-level permission scoping. Consider whether both capabilities are necessary or if one can be restricted.

findings.title: Filesystem access + external network = file exfiltration path
findings.description: Tools that access local files AND make network requests can exfiltrate source code, configs, keys, and documents. Provided by: gzip-file-as-resource (filesystem) + trigger-elicitation-request-async, trigger-elicitation-request, trigger-sampling-request-async, trigger-sampling-request, trigger-url-elicitation (network_external).
findings.recommendation: Implement tool-level permission scoping. Consider whether both capabilities are necessary or if one can be restricted.

findings.title: Code execution + filesystem = unrestricted local access
findings.description: Tools that execute code AND access the filesystem can read/write any file the agent has permissions for, including SSH keys and credentials. Provided by: trigger-long-running-operation (code_execute) + gzip-file-as-resource (filesystem).
findings.recommendation: Implement tool-level permission scoping. Consider whether both capabilities are necessary or if one can be restricted.

findings.title: Memory/context modification capability detected
findings.description: Pattern in __tests__\roots.test.ts near line 131: `session cache`. MCP servers that modify agent memory or context can poison long-term behavior.
findings.recommendation: Validate all data before writing to agent memory. Implement integrity checks on persistent context. Log all memory modifications for audit.

findings.title: Trust exploitation pattern: authority impersonation
findings.description: Pattern in resources\session.ts near line 38: `representing`. This could enable a compromised agent to mislead users.
findings.recommendation: Implement output verification. Require human confirmation for high-impact actions. Mark agent-generated content as such.

findings.title: Trust exploitation pattern: authority impersonation
findings.description: Pattern in resources\templates.ts near line 25: `representing`. This could enable a compromised agent to mislead users.
findings.recommendation: Implement output verification. Require human confirmation for high-impact actions. Mark agent-generated content as such.

findings.title: Trust exploitation pattern: consent bypass
findings.description: Pattern in tools\get-env.ts near line 6: `auto-approve`. This could enable a compromised agent to mislead users.
findings.recommendation: Implement output verification. Require human confirmation for high-impact actions. Mark agent-generated content as such.

findings.title: Runtime tool registration: add_tool('tools/list_changed') in <anonymous>()
findings.description: server\context.ts line 71: the server registers a tool from inside '<anonymous>()' — after the server was approved. A tool that is benign at approval time can be swapped for a malicious one later (rug pull), and a tool injected after the first scan is never reviewed.
findings.recommendation: Register every tool at startup; never mutate the tool list from a tool handler.

findings.title: Blast radius: HIGH — compromise of this server has broad impact
findings.description: If this MCP server is compromised, the blast radius is HIGH due to: arbitrary code execution, external network access, filesystem access, 24 tools (large attack surface), 6 critical findings. A single tool poisoning or supply chain attack could cascade across all connected systems.
findings.recommendation: Apply least-privilege to this server. Isolate it from other MCP servers. Implement kill switches and behavioral monitoring. Limit env vars to the minimum required.

ASI06.name: Memory & Context Poisoning
ASI06.gap_note: Axiom detects static patterns. Full coverage requires runtime memory monitoring.

ASI07.name: Insecure Inter-Agent Communication
ASI07.gap_note: Axiom checks transport security. Full A2A protocol analysis requires runtime interception.

ASI08.name: Cascading Failures
ASI08.gap_note: Axiom estimates blast radius from tool capabilities. Full cascading failure analysis requires runtime topology mapping.

ASI10.name: Rogue Agents
ASI10.gap_note: Axiom detects static rogue indicators. Full rogue agent detection requires runtime behavioral monitoring.

MCP01.name: Token Mismanagement & Secret Exposure
MCP01.reason: Regex-based secret detection in server source and client configs plus env-var exposure checks; no entropy analysis, git-history scan, or token lifetime/passthrough checks.

MCP02.name: Privilege Escalation via Scope Creep
MCP02.reason: Permission over-scope patterns, toxic tool-capability combinations, path-escape checks and env-var over-exposure in configs.

MCP03.name: Tool Poisoning
MCP03.reason: Dedicated detector for hidden instructions in tool metadata, plus runtime rug-pull diffing between source and live tool definitions.

MCP04.name: Software Supply Chain Attacks & Dependency Tampering
MCP04.reason: Dependency CVE lookup, known MCP CVEs, install lifecycle hooks, and unpinned npx/uvx/pip/@latest install sources.

MCP05.name: Command Injection & Execution
MCP05.reason: Regex, AST and Semgrep find exec/shell sinks and a heuristic flags sinks inside tool handlers, but there is no inter-procedural taint tracking from tool input to sink.

MCP06.name: Prompt Injection via Contextual Payloads
MCP06.reason: Injection markers are detected in tool metadata, server instructions, resources, prompts and the strings a tool returns (static), and in instructions/resources/prompts read live; payloads produced by calling a tool at runtime are not inspected.

MCP07.name: Insufficient Authentication & Authorization
MCP07.reason: Flags remote servers with no visible auth and servers bound to all interfaces; does not verify OAuth implementation or per-tool authorization logic.

MCP08.name: Lack of Audit and Telemetry
MCP08.reason: Only a low-confidence heuristic for missing logging in tool-defining files; actual audit trails and telemetry pipelines are not verified.

MCP09.name: Shadow MCP Servers
MCP09.reason: Covered by `axiom discover` allowlist on the local machine; no network-wide or fleet discovery.

MCP10.name: Context Injection & Over-Sharing
MCP10.reason: Hard-coded egress URLs, tools that send to caller-chosen destinations and bulk-exposure heuristics are detected statically and live; what context is actually shared at runtime is not observed.
